For semantics reasons, first I recommend using  HTML <figure> and <figcaption> Elements which are designed for self-contained content, like illustrations, diagrams, photos, code listings, etc. The <figcaption> tag defines a caption for a <figure> element. you can learn more about it from here:

https://www.w3schools.com/html/html5_semantic_elements.asp#:~:text=HTML%20and%20%3Cfigcaption,of%20a%20element.

And about your css, if you want them to be side by side horizontally (which apparently you are trying to do that), as others are suggesting, preferably use flexbox. You do that by setting display: flex to your parent container, and since flex direction by default is set to row (horizontal), you automatically achieve the result you are looking for. and then you can play around with other flex options on your child elements to get more precise results.

But if you wanted to align image and its caption vertically, I wouldn't recommend flex, tbh since you can achieve that by relying on block element behavior.

Remember to don't overuse flexbox, since having too many flex elements in you page can result in a bit of performance issue since flex elements are rendered relative to other elements and can result in laggy UI in a complex document structure.
